Norwegian Oil & Gas Producers Report Stable Output and Modest Growth for First Quarter

Norway’s oil and gas producers posted steady results for the first quarter of the year, as companies benefitted from stable energy prices and continued demand from European markets. According to figures released by the Norwegian Oil Producers Association (NOPA) on Thursday, total production of crude oil and natural gas rose by 2.1 percent compared to the same period last year.

The industry’s overall revenue reached NOK 147 billion, with modest gains attributed to ongoing field developments and efficient operations. “We’re seeing consistent performance across the sector, with producers maintaining reliable output levels and carefully managing costs,” said NOPA director Solveig Jensen. She noted that the Kragerø Basin and Fjordland Shelf fields contributed significantly to the quarter’s results.

Stato Fjell, one of the country’s largest producers, reported a net profit of NOK 18.3 billion for the quarter, citing stable export contracts with EU partners. “Our focus remains on efficiency and safe operations, while pursuing targeted investments in field maintenance,” said CEO Olav Eriksen.

Analysts at NordVest Markets described the results as “solid and unspectacular,” emphasizing the absence of major disruptions or price volatility. “Norwegian producers are in a favourable position due to long-term contracts and a reputation for reliability,” said senior analyst Ragnhild Borgen.

Employment levels in the sector held steady, with around 52,000 workers directly employed, according to the Norwegian Offshore Workers Union. “Stable output means secure jobs for our members,” said union leader Janne Moen.

NOPA representatives said the outlook for the remainder of the year remains positive, as European demand for Norwegian gas continues to underpin the industry’s performance. The industry is also preparing for its annual general meeting in Stavanger next month, where sustainability initiatives and digitalization are expected to be key topics.
